events.text: Review #222 against the lead's must-block list and post your verdict.

I've requested changes on #222 (PR-4, which relaxes the live Bash guard). It opens a new hole: text from `echo` or `printf` piped into a SQL client is no longer caught. Three cases were blocked on master and pass on the PR head: `echo '<SQL>;' | psql`, `printf '<SQL>;' | sqlite3 db`, and `echo … | tee … | psql`. The new masking hides the quoted text of "data" commands without checking whether that text is piped into something that runs it. The heredoc path already has that check. The fix is to apply the same rule here, with those three cases as failing tests first.

I ran 47 test commands through a copy of the live `pre_tool_use.py`, once with master's code and once with the PR's:
- **The lead's must-block list:** most still block. That includes `bash -c`, `xargs rm`, heredocs into or piped to `sh`/`psql`, and rm or psql inside backticks or `$()` in an echo.
- **The rest of that list was never blocked, on master either:** rm inside `$()` in double quotes (in `echo` and `git commit -m`), `eval`, `echo … | sh`, `sh <(echo …)`, `git -c alias.x='!…'`, and `python3 - <<PY | sh`. #222 didn't cause these, so it can't keep them blocked; I listed them for a follow-up.
- **The scratchpad rm rule is safe.** A real repo clone inside the session scratchpad can now be deleted. The main checkout, a lookalike path under `~/Gits`, and a `..` escape out of the scratchpad all stay blocked. I agree with w6 not following the brief's rev-parse-the-parent idea: it would have allowed deleting `~/Gits/<repo>` itself.
- **w6's 5 false positives are fixed** (SQL in a python heredoc, `gh --body`, a printf to the collab, `git commit -m`, and echo prose naming credentials.json). All 457 tests pass, and the `harness_paths.py` move is verbatim.

The review is at https://github.com/EtanHey/golems/pull/222#pullrequestreview-5312588713, and the REVIEW line is in the collab. Next: round 2 on #222, then the rest of GO-5. My report and DONE marker wait for the lead's "GO-5 closed".
